He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2}} and {{convert|225|lb|0}}, he plays the [[small forward]] position. Okoro played basketball for [[McEachern High School]] in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] for four years, helping his team win the state championship and achieve national success in his senior season. He was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports]] and [[ESPN]]. After his freshman college season at [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], he was named to the second team All-SEC. ==Early life== Okoro was born in [[Atlanta]], Georgia to Nigerian parents and was raised in [[metro Atlanta]]. His father, Godwin, emigrated from [[Nigeria]] in the 1980s. His mother, Gloria, is also from Nigeria.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan|title=Isaac Okoro: 2019 Hoop Summit Interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jo4xHsN9bTk |website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=April 11, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} Okoro started playing basketball in his local church league. When he was around seven to eight years old, he began training under the guidance of [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) coach Omar Cooper, the father of his future high school teammate, [[Sharife Cooper]]. He played for the A.O.T. Running Rebels of the Nike EYBL circuit.{{cite web |last=Scarborough |first=Alex |date=February 12, 2020 |title=Auburn back to the Final Four? Only if Isaac Okoro gets selfish |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28679298 |access-date=February 21, 2020 |website=[[ESPN]]}} ==High school career== Okoro played high school basketball for [[McEachern High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]]. In his freshman season, he averaged 15 points and eight rebounds per game, helping his team win the regional title and reach the [[Georgia High School Association]] Class 7A state quarterfinals.{{cite Montgomery Advertiser|language=en-US}} ===Recruiting=== By the end of his high school career, Okoro was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports]] and [[ESPN]].{{cite web |title=Isaac Okoro |url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isaac-okoro/14897 |publisher=Auburn University Athletics |access-date=April 29, 2020}}{{cite web |date=March 20, 2020 |title=Auburn freshman Isaac Okoro to declare eligibility for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28933596 |access-date=April 29, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On July 25, 2018, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], among others.{{cite web |url=https://www.oanow.com/sports/college/auburn/isaac-okoro-ranked-th-nationally-in-class-commits-to-auburn/article_87d90eb6-8fc9-11e8-bf4b-03c5d7b184b7.html |website=[[Opelika-Auburn News]] bball = yes }} ==College career== Okoro scored 12 points in his Auburn debut, a 84–73 win over [[2019–20 Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball team|Georgia Southern]]. The following game, he registered 17 points in a 76–66 victory over [[2019–20 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]].{{cite news |last=Vitale |first=Josh |title=Auburn's 'most talented |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2019/11/12/auburn-basketball-freshman-isaac-okoro-living-up-to-the-hype-south-alabama-preview-mobile-nba-draft/2561947001/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |date=November 12, 2019}} Okoro was named [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Freshman of the Week on November 18, 2019.{{Cite No. 5 Auburn edge Vanderbilt 83–79 to stay perfect |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/08/okoro-no-5-auburn-edge-vanderbilt-83-79-to-stay-perfect/ |access-date=January 9, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 8, 2020}} He did not play in a February 15 game against [[2019–20 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] due to a [[Pulled hamstring|hamstring injury]].{{cite news|title=Smith, Pinson lead Missouri to 85–73 win over No. 11 Auburn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166350 |access-date=February 16, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 15, 2020}} After the regular season, he was named to the All-SEC Second Team, the SEC All-Freshman Team and the SEC All-Defensive Team by the league's coaches.{{Cite web|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards|title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=March 10, 2020}} Okoro averaged 12.9 points, 4.4 rebounds and two assists per game. After his freshman season, he announced that he would enter the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Boone |first=Kyle |title=Auburn freshman Isaac Okoro, projected lottery pick, set to test NBA Draft waters |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/auburn-freshman-isaac-okoro-projected-lottery-pick-set-to-test-nba-draft-waters/ |access-date=March 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 20, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2020–2025)=== Okoro was selected with the fifth pick overall by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Adams|title=Cavaliers Select Isaac Okoro with Fifth Overall Pick In 2020 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/okoro-selection-201118|website=NBA.com|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 18, 2020}} Three days later on November 21, the Cavaliers announced that they had signed Okoro.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Adams|title=Cavaliers Sign 2020 NBA Draft Pick Isaac Okoro|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/okoro-signing-20121|website=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2020|access-date=November 21, 2020}} In the Cavaliers' first preseason game of the [[2020–21 NBA season]], he scored the game-winning [[and-one]] to make it 114–116 and converted the [[free throw]] to make it 114–117 and win against the [[2020–21 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]]. On December 23, 2020, Okoro made his [[NBA]] debut, starting and recording 11 points, five assists, and three rebounds in a 121–114 win over the [[2020–21 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Penix|title=Cavs: 3 takeaways from season opener win|url=https://cavsnation.com/cavs-3-takeaways-from-season-opener-win/|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=December 24, 2020|access-date=December 25, 2020}} On May 4, 2021, he scored a career-high 32 points during a 134–118 overtime loss to the [[2020–21 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Withers|title=BOOKER SCORES 31, SUNS DOMINATE OT TO BEAT CAVS 134-118|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-cle-0022000983undefined|website=NBA.com|date=May 4, 2021|access-date=November 9, 2023}} On March 23, 2023, Okoro had one rebound, one assist, and scored 11 points, including a game-winning three-pointer, in a 116–114 win over the [[2022–23 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web | title=Okoro's 3-pointer sends Cavaliers past Nets 116-114 | website=ABC7 New York | date=2023-03-24 | url=https://abc7ny.com/post/okoros-3-pointer-sends-cavaliers-past-nets-116-114/13000713/?userab=abc_web_player-460*variant_a_abc_control-1900%2Cotv_web_player-461*variant_a_otv_control-1902%2Cotv_web_content_rec-445*variant_a_control-1849%2Chp_banner-426*variant_b_arrow-1778 | access-date=2025-12-09}} On September 17, 2024, Okoro signed a three-year, $33 million contract with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Isaac Okoro to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-isaac-okoro-re-sign-240917|website=NBA.com|date=September 17, 2024|access-date=September 17, 2024}} ===Chicago Bulls (2025–present)=== On July 6, 2025, Okoro was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Lonzo Ball]].{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bulls acquire Isaac Okoro from Cleveland Cavaliers {{!}} Chicago Bulls |url=https://bulls.com/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-isaac-okoro-from-cleveland-cavaliers |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=bulls.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Okoro played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in Argentina.
